rationales.wacc: 11.5% (analyst judgment; no market-data series in the snapshot). Cost of equity = assumed risk-free rate of about 4.25% + assumed beta of about 1.5 x assumed equity risk premium of 5% = about 11.75%. Beta is set above the market because AMD's revenue is concentrated in a cyclical, AI-capex-driven Data Center ramp, a small number of customers account for a substantial part of revenue (periodic.txt forward-looking statement list), and export restrictions already affect Instinct MI308 (Q-8). Debt is a negligible share of capital: aggregate principal $7.1B (F-4539257085) against a market capitalisation of about $794B (last close $483.90 on 2026-11-03 x 1,640M cover-page shares). After-tax cost of debt is roughly 4.5% (August 2026 notes priced at 4.600%-5.500%, periodic.txt Note 9, less 13% tax), so the blend rounds to 11.5%. This is within the gate band [6%, 16%].
rationales.terminal_growth: 3.0%: a long-run nominal growth rate roughly in line with nominal GDP. It is below the year-5 revenue growth of 8%, so the model fades into the terminal period. A higher rate would assume AMD's share of a structurally growing compute market keeps rising indefinitely, which I do not assume. Within the gate band [0, 4%].
rationales.revenue_growth: Year 1 is code-derived NTM revenue (FY2026Q4-FY2027Q3 from assumptions.json, about $73.1B, roughly +61% on TTM revenue of $45.4B, i.e. D-da671c66c3 + F-e8860f2d21 + F-0c22036940 + F-6fa20ae3f8). Years 2-5: 25%, 18%, 12% and 8% (analyst judgment). The steep fade from the year-1 rate reflects: (a) year 1 already includes the guided +27% Q4 step-up (Q-1) and the MI450/Helios ramp (Q-6); (b) the customer-warrant programmes (periodic.txt, two customers, up to 160M shares each, vesting on purchase milestones) indicate multi-year committed deployments that support above-market growth in years 2-3; (c) cyclicality of AI capex, customer concentration and export restrictions (Q-8) argue against extrapolating; (d) Client & Gaming declined year over year in the release. Year-5 revenue is about $142B.
rationales.fcf_margin: FCF = CFO - capex (mapped cfo and capex lines) relative to revenue, rising from 18% in year 1 to 24% in year 5. History: TTM through FY2026Q3 = (2,600 + 2,955 + 2,366 + 1,202 - 222 - 389 - 808 - 648) / 45,436 = 15.5% ($M; CFO D-cdf03a9bf1, F-5faa172c8d, D-1fac18eb03, D-161017865b; capex D-51afa34bd4, F-8f8008f21d, D-91a4e4886f, D-91daa3cfaa). FY2025 (four quarters through FY2025Q4) = (7,709 - 974) / 34,639 = 19.4%, but that CFO includes $920M of discontinued ZT Manufacturing operating cash for 9M2025 (periodic.txt MD&A), so continuing-operations FY2025 is about 16.8%. Individual quarters ranged from 4.1% (FY2026Q3) to 25.0% (FY2026Q1). The recent low is driven by working capital: in 9M2026 operating assets and liabilities absorbed $3.6B (inventory +$3.5B for the Data Center ramp, receivables +$2.9B, supply prepayments +$2.1B, partly offset by payables +$4.5B; periodic.txt). Before working capital, 9M2026 CFO less capex was about (6,523 + 3,631 - 1,845) / 35,166 = 23.6%. Year 1 (18%) sits between the TTM and the pre-working-capital rate because NTM revenue grows about 61% and will need further inventory and receivables. Capex has stepped up (9M2026 $1.8B vs $0.8B) and is assumed to stay near 5% of revenue. Margins then rise toward the pre-working-capital level (24% in year 5) as growth slows to 8% and the working-capital drag shrinks. The forecast GAAP net margin (NTM net income about $17.0B on $73.1B, about 23%, from assumptions.json) plus non-cash intangible amortisation (about $2.2B a year) and SBC (about $2.1B a year at the current run-rate, D-5fe6261c71) less capex is consistent with 24% before working capital. Caveats: FCF here treats SBC as non-cash (it adds back about 4% of revenue), and the 9M2026 cash tax bill was reduced by stock-compensation deductions that may not recur.
rationales.peers: NVDA, AVGO, MRVL and INTC: the covered companies whose main business, like AMD's, is designing compute or data-center silicon (GPUs/accelerators, CPUs, custom AI ASICs and networking). Excluded: MU (memory, a commodity-priced business with a different cycle), AMAT, LRCX and KLAC (wafer-fab equipment), SNPS and CDNS (EDA software with software margins), MPWR (power management), and ALAB and CRDO (small-cap connectivity names; revenue under $2B and EV/Sales above 17x, which would skew a median for a company with $45B of revenue). INTC is kept as the direct x86 CPU competitor even though it is loss-making on a TTM basis. EV/Sales uses it because EV/Sales does not need positive earnings. At the cutoff, TTM EV/Sales is about 16.5x NVDA, 18.2x AVGO, 16.1x MRVL and 5.8x INTC (code median about 16.3x). TTM ends for NVDA, AVGO and MRVL fall in July-August 2026, within 120 days of AMD's 2026-09-26, and INTC's TTM end matches AMD's.
rationales.dcf_weight: 0.7 DCF / 0.3 peer EV/Sales. The DCF carries the case-specific forecast (the guided Q4 step-up and the GAAP bridge in assumptions.json). The peer method uses trailing revenue, which understates AMD at a time when NTM revenue is about 61% above TTM. The peer set is also dispersed (about 5.8x to 18.2x), so the median depends heavily on which names are included. The peer value is still useful as a market cross-check on the DCF's terminal-value-heavy result, so it keeps a 30% weight rather than zero.
